role: v4 target orchestration contract; implementation and execution must be verified separately
origin: plugins/evidence-lane-plugin/toolchains/tool-definitions.v4.json and the accepted v4 workflow corrections; historical imported hashes remain in the definition provenance

public_workflows.rule: Original retained first-class skills remain separate, each owning its actual multiple actions; no fixed six-workflow partition.

orchestration_layers.role: Codex interprets user intent through first-class skills; Windows Studio is the persistent connection/orchestration app with a read-only human view.
Codex Desktop, CLI and supported VM hosts use native MCP clients; optional authenticated remote clients use a declared remote engine
One action registry produces SDK/MCP/skill/hook contracts; supported host events only
Resolve project, current Plan revision, dependencies, source scope, lane contract and information versus semantic steer
Agent selects an eligible lane/action route; engine enforces declared primary/fallback order, permissions, readiness, compatibility, budgets and external configuration
Persistent engine coordinates bounded jobs and prewarmed workers with one writer per project; CPU/CUDA/ROCm/DirectML is a shared execution-provider choice
Validate operation-specific outputs and checks; reconcile effects, append receipts, update derived views, and reject stale worker completion
After a verified Delta exit, update project-local Learning and select the next ready task; preserve attributed Memory, Canon and ChatLineage separately

mcp_transport_and_composition: OpenAI Agents SDK typed tools and MCP utilities without another agent owner

mcp_role_taxonomy.hosts_and_clients: Codex and other explicitly supported connecting clients; observed connection state is separate from claimed host identity
mcp_role_taxonomy.server_transport_frameworks: MCP Python SDK and FastMCP are implementation frameworks, not connected Codex clients
mcp_role_taxonomy.native_local_tools: Git, parsers, renderers and local libraries remain tools rather than MCP clients
mcp_role_taxonomy.compute_providers: CPU, NVIDIA and AMD execution readiness is independent of client or connector connection state

optional_extensions.role: Additional or configured external connectors, plugins and toolchain grants; not the core toolchain matrix
optional_extensions.execution: Eligible only inside a selected operation and current grant; presence never means execute all tools

steer_handling.informational: Bounded read-only answer; no Plan mutation
steer_handling.semantic: Checkpoint or cancel affected work, atomically replace current/queued contracts, preserve completed history, reject stale completion and resume eligible work

storage.per_project: One selected external project root; each authority and sector owns separate SQLite, schema history and files; Root PV coordinates exact lane heads.
storage.derived_files: Separate per-lane folders retain each contract's own subset and semantics for MMD, DOT, pointers and natural artifacts
storage.cross_project: Explicit in-place read-only queries with attribution; no database merging

studio.layout: Direct HIL four-shell reuse: project side rail, persistent top context shell, workflow pills in command/prompt bar, single changing inner content panel.
studio.toolchains: Filter by lane, operation and orchestration layer; show ordered eligible tools, selected route, fallback reason and actual readiness
studio.connections: Separate host/client sessions from MCP tool providers and optional connectors
studio.status: Live data only; placeholders and target mockups are labelled, unavailable features do not display fabricated active state
studio.visibility: Visible in development and shipping; open, minimize and reopen while the engine can run in the background
studio.reuse_mode: Actual components and theme implementation, with adapted v4 bindings and provenance; not visual imitation only.
studio.pairing_order: Complete the executable plugin first, then pair this separate app.

workers.role: Execute the selected toolchain with bounded resources and attributed process/operation evidence.

installation.local: Provision all required retained local libraries, binaries, model assets and supported provider environments with Studio/engine.
installation.external: Ship adapters; configure external services and credentials explicitly.
installation.execution: Installation does not execute every tool; lane/operation primary and fallback routing remains conditional.
installation.direct_codex_use: Resolve explicit executable/environment paths from the same verified shared Studio installation

host_platform_policy.Windows: Studio/backend with its shared managed toolchain; execution requires measured readiness and lane selection.
host_platform_policy.macOS: MCP/SDK/skills/hooks host path only; no local Studio or Windows-managed toolchain capabilities. Current direct adapter implementation and host support must be verified.
host_platform_policy.mobile: No Studio application or mobile product workflow.
host_platform_policy.VM_and_CLI: Use the host matrix and explicit supported backend route; ephemeral hosts need verified persistent storage.
host_platform_policy.tool_count: Derive counts from the current registry; installed and usable counts come from runtime evidence.

command_path: Studio persistent backend API on a supported route
Codex result and read-only Studio view
purge: Final cross-layer purge after replacement implementation and Studio pairing; record each retained feature location and each removal reason.
